title: Employer job flow does not stand in for primary-care adequacy
source_unit: US county-sector BDS flows overlaid with represented designated primary-care HPSA components
geography: United States; county-sector rows with 2023 BDS rates and current HRSA county-FIPS representation

observations.period: 2023; health care and social assistance; county with represented designated primary-care HPSA component
observations.method: Descriptive overlay of 2023 BDS county-sector rates with current HRSA primary-care HPSA county-FIPS representation.
observations.uncertainty: HPSA components can be geographic, population-based, facility-based, or partial-county; current designation timing is not a frozen 2023 treatment, and job flow is not provider capacity.
observations.subgroup: Health-care-and-social-assistance rows in counties with at least one represented designated primary-care HPSA component.
observations.counterinterpretation: A positive median job-flow rate coexists with a substantial negative-net share and does not establish usable care.

observations.period: 2023; health care and social assistance; county without represented designated primary-care HPSA component
observations.method: Descriptive overlay of 2023 BDS county-sector rates with current HRSA primary-care HPSA county-FIPS representation.
observations.uncertainty: Absence of represented HPSA components is not proof of adequate care; neighboring providers, designation timing, and component coverage are not fully observed.
observations.subgroup: Health-care-and-social-assistance rows without represented designated primary-care HPSA components.
observations.counterinterpretation: The higher median in the nonrepresented group does not establish better access, because employer flow and HPSA designation measure different stages.

observations.period: 2023; selected-sector HPSA versus other county comparison

denominator.unit: county FIPS represented by at least one designated primary-care HPSA component

observations.method: Cross-vintage descriptive comparison; HPSA county representation is a designation surface, not a county-wide shortage treatment.
observations.uncertainty: The HPSA and BDS universes, vintages, and component boundaries differ; no resident-level or causal inference is attempted.
observations.subgroup: Selected BDS sectors split by current HRSA primary-care HPSA county representation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sector differences vary by sector and cannot be reduced to a single capacity gradient.

boundary: This is a cross-vintage descriptive overlay. HPSA component presence is not county-wide shortage, and BDS job flow is not provider adequacy, care use, or household outcome.
